notes.title: A ship is safest in the harbor, but that’s not what ships are for. DevLog#6
notes.content:
[p]Hello,
This is SavePoint.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/33f82eea4fdb03de838530a35d302bd4885c872b.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b]We've had an especially busy month.
[/b]As we are conducting an offline playtest with 20 real users, we've been racing to finish everything we’ve built so far. Though we've worked hard, packaging everything up is revealing some unexpected issues.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/d7b3dd221b362a82636ffcf8b0757be401a43f35.gif"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]Still, our game has made great progress.[/b]
Skills for tier 5 and 6 developers have been added (though still a bit rough), and effects for the furniture that helps developers are now implemented. It's a great stage for testing. Once we touch up the recipe window for automated combinations and tweak the level design to make the game more fun, we’ll be ready.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/04b88c2107de2ac6ebce0cd4d733ffb24ad496d8.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b]We’re aiming for a busy game.[/b]
We hope players can feel the hectic pace of game development, and experience its metaphors through our game.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Thank you.[/p]

notes.title: Easy Come, Easy Go. DevLog #5
notes.content:
[p]Hello,
This is SavePoint on yet another fine day.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/27e785d3e2179db51fc7d17d88ef5c9575b8adb6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We have been steadily making progress.[/p][p][b]DevLog List[/b][/p][list][*][p]Added backend for the card system usable during defense[/p][/*][*][p]Backend to track the player’s current developer state for providing an auto-combination chart[/p][/*][*][p]Added skills and skill animations for Tier 6 developers[/p][/*][*][p]Redesigned shop layout (as shown in the image above)[/p][/*][*][p]New developer combination recipes[/p][/*][*][p]And more+++[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]This is a skill prototype for the “Dragon” character.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/67c300d92fef4f775ffd762b3ad2eaae8835dc92.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We continue to work hard to bring out the game’s [i]core fun[/i].
Once the game is complete, we hope to share it with players from various countries around the world! We will keep developing with the hope that one day people everywhere will enjoy playing our game.[/p]

notes.title: The Sweetest Moment of the Day Lies in the Early Morning. DevLog#4
notes.content:
[p]Hello,
This is SavePoint.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/87a93f93e2ea716f3fb97f587f8f748eca921565.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]This week, I’ve decided to take a break from the weekly devlog.[/b]
I was just getting the hang of writing development diaries and thinking of trying to write more engaging entries by topic, but work is just too hectic right now.[/p][p][/p][p]They say those who manage their time well are the ones who succeed,
but I guess I’ll be the one who learns through failure.[/p][p][/p][p]I’ll be back with development updates in the next DevLog.[/p]

notes.title: While There’s Life, There’s Hope. DevLog#3
notes.content:
[p]Hello,
This is SavePoint’s DevLog #3.[/p][p]As we develop our game, we want to discuss a different topic each time. Today’s topic comes from our experience applying to the SGM indie game support program.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/396fc6f9829210577624034b0002c3ff8a7eb94b.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]“How much should you show in a build?”[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Most developers want to show off everything they’ve made. But that’s not always the best approach. You might worry, “If I include all the highlights, will people just enjoy the best parts and lose interest in buying the full game?” Or, “This weapon is meant for the late game and is too strong—should I really show it in a one-hour demo?”
This leads to two main approaches:[/p][list][*][p]Show as much as possible of what you’ve developed[/p][/*][*][p]Focus on the actual game progression and help players concentrate on the intended experience[/p][/*][/list][p]We faced the same dilemma. We chose to show as much as possible, but realized that wasn’t ideal. Our tutorial became too long, and many players missed out on key features, leading to a less enjoyable experience.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Our conclusion:[/b]
Focus on the game’s [b]core fun[/b].[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/bdb76bcf98cb6061f0449bcc77a20fe4559761c5.png"][/img][/p][p]Our game is a pool-building game disguised as a defense game. As rounds progress, players build their own pools in limited space to maximize efficiency. The core is letting players experience building their unique pool.[/p][p][/p][p]Key features to showcase:[/p][list][*][p]Developer skills[/p][/*][*][p]Furniture effects[/p][/*][*][p](A few directive cards)[/p][/*][*][p]And... limited space![/p][/*][*][p]Plus, active offense features for player-driven farming[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]You should design a minimal number of rounds that let players experience these core features and observe their reactions. As a developer, it’s natural to feel regret about features you can’t show. That’s okay! At the end of the demo, you can always mention upcoming features on the closing screen. If your core systems are fun, players will look forward to what’s next.[/p][p][/p][p]I hope one day we can show this game to everyone reading this, now or in the future.
Keep fighting![/p][p][/p][p]From,
SavePoint[/p]

notes.title: We Cannot Change the Direction of the Wind, But We Can Adjust the Sails
notes.content:
[h3]Hello,
This is SavePoint.[/h3][p][/p][p]We wanted to write a fun announcement, but it didn’t quite work out. We thought about making a quiz, but with AI, all the answers would be too easy to find. We also considered puns, but couldn’t come up with jokes that would work in multiple languages, so we gave up. Instead, we’d like to share some behind-the-scenes stories from our development. We’ll go in reverse order, starting with the most recent events and working back to when we first started making games. Hopefully, by the time we talk about our very first game development experience, our current project will be finished and released![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/2451cf5dcf89c46158182158073aa924fd7cf1ba.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]\[Game Development Story on June 23rd][/b][/h3][p]Just yesterday, on June 23rd, we received the acceptance notice for the Smilegate Membership. Smilegate is the company behind the FPS game “Crossfire,” which was especially popular in China. They have a foundation that supports indie game developers, selecting teams each year to provide support. We heard that about 160 teams applied this time, and our team was selected!
We’ve applied to support programs like this before, but always fell short due to the completeness of our game. Could this successful application be the signal for even better things to come?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/2057eb1d1d37aa3f716fb1c77115e5f925a91c1c.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45568873/201be98ab9784678407d994952f738d2ae6f51a6.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Two Weeks of Work[/b][/h3][p]Over the past two weeks, we’ve focused on supplementing areas that weren’t included in our previous build. The build we had was only about a quarter of what we originally intended, so we’re now adding features that were left out. These additions include implementing the effects of furniture that help the developer character during the programming phase. With these effects and the ability to adjust the size of the office, the game will become even more exciting. Please look forward to our future development updates![/p][p][/p][p]Summer is just around the corner here in Korea.
Take care of your health, and we wish you wonderful days ahead.[/p][p][/p][p]From,
SavePoint[/p]

notes.title: The Days Are Getting Hotter, and Our Development Passion Is Rising
notes.content:
[p]Hello, everyone who is interested in GOTY.[/p][p][/p][p]We have registered GOTY on Steam in preparation for a grant application. Although it was initially just for show, surprisingly, a few users have wishlisted and checked out our game. Some even left comments on the community, saying they liked the game’s images.[/p][p][/p][p][b]As developers, we are truly amazed by this interest—and deeply grateful.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]We have been busy lately creating a build for the grant program. We want to share it with those who are interested in our game, but the current build is not quite ready for release yet.[/p][p]From now on, we plan to make our Steam page more accessible and update various artworks. We will also post development logs at least once every two weeks to keep you updated on our progress. Since we are a team of three, there may be times when progress is slow due to various circumstances, but we believe it’s important to keep you informed regardless.[/p][p][/p][p]We will also think about ways to make our development updates more interesting.[/p][h3][b]Thank you to everyone who seeks out small indie games and takes the time to check out ours.[/b]ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3][p][/p][p]Best regards,
SavePoint, the GOTY Development Team[/p]
